how: Missed memos and suspected reversed fixes support incomplete coordination but do not demonstrate identified keepers erasing an agreed change or that change being abandoned.
The report of uninformed randoms supports a communication difficulty but leaves the added mechanism of repairing agreed changes away unresolved.
Border violations cannot automatically be explained as uninformed repair when participants explicitly contest the compromise and demand removal of the border.
The information-deficit mechanism requires evidence of keeper knowledge because different repair targets alone cannot distinguish ignorance, dissent, or behaviour after an instruction.
Continuing the old background does not establish uninformed restoration, since voluntary coordination, authority dissent, and stated preferences leave informed disagreement possible.
Continued opposition cannot be explained solely by missing instructions when informed members dispute the agreement or reject the concession.
The repair account supports perceived hostile changes being undone without establishing room agreement, failed notification or permanent loss of the revision.
The added repair mechanism is supported as mistaken resistance, but later visual recognition does not establish notification or eventual loss from failed communication.
Variant resistance establishes a disputed maintenance target but does not establish that keepers unknowingly reverse an agreed change or abandon it when uninformed.
The repair misunderstanding concerns a neighbour's intended overlap rather than a demonstrated change already agreed by the room.
Explaining disputed border changes as uninformed repair requires evidence that keepers lacked notice, which objection to the terms alone does not supply.
Informing keepers can correct mistaken repair but cannot alone reconcile deliberate allegiance to a template that conflicts with negotiated commitments.
Attributing resistance to uninformed repair requires evidence of an adopted change and uninformed keepers, while the visible keeper explicitly rejects the displayed border plan.
Information can correct mistaken repairs, but informed holdouts can reject an approved change after knowing of it.
Treat failed communication as permanent loss only when the outcome is evidenced, since these passages establish mistaken repair and announced restraint rather than every change's eventual fate.
Defence is supported, but attributing conflict to keepers undoing agreed changes requires identified repair behaviour rather than delayed news, random damage or intentional expansion alone.
Sleeping operators and stale scripts show a communication risk but not an observed agreed redesign repaired away or abandoned.
An updated target does not establish the revised claim that uninformed keepers reverse planned changes or cause their abandonment.
Applying the added known-form repair explanation requires evidence of keepers erasing an agreed change, which delayed reading of terms alone does not supply.
Repeated repair of a planned change establishes interference, not inevitable permanent abandonment whenever informing some keepers fails.
Failed accommodation can follow explicit refusal of an announced agreement and reported preference for overwriting rather than only keepers lacking design information.
Limit local instantiation to observed defense and requested communication because no passage establishes keepers erasing an agreed change or losing it through failed notification.
Disputed border terms support competing repair targets but do not establish that an agreed change failed specifically because notification did not reach keepers.
